root_cause.text: The as102_usb_probe() function directly frees the as102_dev_t structure via kfree() on the error path after usb_register_dev() has succeeded, without accounting for the possibility that userspace may have already opened a file descriptor that will later invoke the .release() callback and attempt to free the same structure again.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the kfree() call from the error path after usb_deregister_dev() and adds `return ret;` instead, deferring memory deallocation to the .release() callback. The CVE description explicitly states: "The fix is to never kfree(as102_dev_t) directly once usb_register_dev() has succeeded. After deregistration, defer freeing memory to .release()." This demonstrates that the vulnerability stems from premature freeing in the probe error path while open file descriptors still reference the device structure, leading to use-after-free and double-free conditions when those descriptors are later closed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix error handling in as102_usb_probe by clearing interface data before deregistration and returning early from failed_stream to prevent redundant cleanup and resource leaks.
intent_record.what: Added two lines in the failed_stream error handling path: (1) usb_set_intfdata(intf, NULL) before usb_deregister_dev(), and (2) return ret; after usb_deregister_dev(). This causes the function to return early from the failed_stream label instead of falling through to the failed label.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that when the stream buffer allocation fails, the interface data is properly cleared before deregistering the device, and the function returns immediately with the error code rather than continuing to the failed label where usb_put_dev() and another usb_set_intfdata() call would execute. This prevents redundant cleanup operations and ensures proper error propagation.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function shows the error path at lines 415-421. Line 416 calls usb_deregister_dev(intf, &as102_usb_class_driver) which deregisters the device, but line 420 directly calls kfree(as102_dev) to free the structure. The vulnerability exists because usb_register_dev() (called earlier in the probe function, not shown) may have allowed userspace to open a file descriptor. When usb_deregister_dev() is called, it does not prevent the .release() callback from being invoked later by the kernel when userspace closes that file descriptor. The .release() callback will then attempt to free the same as102_dev structure that was already freed at line 420, causing a double-free. The fix would require using usb_put_dev() or reference counting to defer the kfree() until after all file descriptors are closed, rather than immediately freeing the structure in the error path.
